notices.format: Fixed statutory form with a To: line and an (INSERT ADDRESS) blank, either incorporated conspicuously in a written contract or sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, before commencing work
notices.support: either incorporated conspicuously in a written contract or sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, any time prior to commencing work or delivery of materials
notices.summary_row: NOTICE OF POSSIBLE MECHANIC'S LIEN (lien chapter version) and indemnity
notices.hold_reason: the only copies of this notice sit inside whole statute sections (34-28-4.1 and 5-65-3 subsections k to p) that carry operative rules, fines and indemnity around the notice, and the two copies differ in commas and one plural, so printing a block would put non-notice statute text in the contract

notices.title: Statement that the contractor, subcontractors or materialpersons may file a lien
notices.trigger: Every written contract between a registered contractor and a property owner
notices.format: No wording prescribed; a statement in the contract
notices.support: No wording is prescribed for this statement; no formatting rule.
notices.summary_row: Lien statement in every written contract
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the statute only lists required content

notices.format: Notice to buyer in ten-point bold-face type or larger directly above the buyer's signature space, then a Notice of Cancellation under that conspicuous caption; registered or certified mail; the statute prints both three days and three business days, and the chapter defines business day (Sundays and postal holidays skipped, Saturday counts)
notices.support: in ten-point (10), bold-face type or larger directly above the space reserved in the agreement for the signature of the buyer
notices.summary_row: "Notice to buyer" (10 point bold above signature) and "Notice of Cancellation"
notices.hold_reason: the block is the whole of 6-28-4, which also holds the seller's duty to return a deposit within 20 days and double damages, so printing it would put non-notice statute text in the contract

notices.trigger: In-home solicitation of an elderly person for contractor work at the consumer's primary residence, including telephonic or online, except transactions the consumer initiated
notices.format: Separate Notice of Cancellation under the conspicuous caption, worded 'this agreement' and 'consumer's signing' (not the 6-28-4 wording)
notices.support: except those transactions initiated by the consumer
notices.summary_row: Elderly person in-home solicitation Notice of Cancellation
notices.hold_reason: the block is the whole of 5-65-27 (definitions, the three day rule and the deposit refund rule around the notice), and the age that makes a person elderly is in 42-66-4.1, which the file did not fetch

notices.support: NOT OBTAINED: no such text exists in either active Board regulation
notices.summary_row: "Consumer disclosures and information required pursuant to regulations promulgated by the board" (5-65-3(o))

changes.new: Three days counted as calendar days, skipping Sundays and postal holidays, by registered or certified mail; the statutory notice prints both 'three days' and 'three business days' as written
changes.support: count calendar days, skip Sundays and postal holidays; SATURDAY COUNTS

changes.new: Count calendar days, skip Sundays and postal holidays; Saturday counts (6-28-2(1) defines business day this way, so the statute's three days and three business days mean the same count).
changes.support: count calendar days, skip Sundays and postal holidays; SATURDAY COUNTS

changes.new: Door-to-door sales of consumer goods or services of $25 or more, including visits the buyer invited, as 6-28-2 defines them, on top of the federal rule
changes.support: in response to, or following an invitation by, the buyer

unsure: RI-cancel: the 6-28-4 block is a whole section with a deposit refund rule in subsection (d) around the two notices, so it is held rather than printed.

RI-62: the age that makes a person elderly is in 42-66-4.1, which the file did not fetch, and the builder does not know buyer age, so this would be on_file at best; it is held because the block is the whole 5-65-27 section.
RI-lien: both copies of the lien notice are inside whole statute sections with operative text, so none is loaded even though two official copies exist.

RI-board: the Board flyer (agency guidance, not law) may be the Summary of Registration Law that 5-65-3(k) says is handed to the owner when work begins, but the file only quotes its insurance paragraph, so it is not loaded.
RI-lien-statement: added because 5-65-18 puts a lien statement in every written contract, but the statute prescribes no sentence.
